intent.raw_query: Seoul K-culture and food, $2200 couple, winter 2026 from LAX

selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Seoul, South Korea

experiences.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Experience
experiences.description: Explore the grand Joseon-era Gyeongbokgung Palace while dressed in a traditional Hanbok rental. Wearing Hanbok grants free palace entry, and you can stroll through the historic grounds, visit the National Folk Museum inside, and capture stunning photos at the iconic gates. A deeply immersive K-culture and history experience.

experiences.name: Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into one of Seoul's oldest and most beloved traditional markets. Sample iconic Korean street foods including bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap (addictive mini rice rolls), tteokbokki, and fresh yukhoe (beef tartare). Interact with local vendors and experience the vibrant, authentic food culture that has thrived here for over a century.

experiences.name: K-Pop Idol Dance Class
experiences.description: Take a professional K-pop dance lesson at one of Hongdae's many dedicated dance academies. Learn choreography from popular idol groups taught by trained instructors. This hands-on experience is perfect for K-culture enthusiasts and gives a behind-the-scenes look at the training culture that produces world-famous K-pop stars.

experiences.name: Insadong Cultural Alley & Tea House Visit
experiences.description: Wander through Insadong's charming alleyways filled with traditional craft shops, calligraphy studios, antique galleries, and indie boutiques. End your stroll with a visit to a traditional Korean tea house (dawon) to enjoy a ceremonial cup of omija or barley tea paired with tteok (rice cakes). A serene and culturally rich afternoon experience.

experiences.name: Korean BBQ Dinner Experience in Mapo
experiences.description: Enjoy an authentic Korean BBQ dinner at a local grill restaurant in the Mapo district, a favorite among locals. Grill samgyeopsal (pork belly) and chadolbaegi (beef brisket) at your table, wrap them in perilla leaves with ssamjang paste, and pair with unlimited banchan (side dishes) and a glass of soju or makgeolli. A quintessential and social Korean dining ritual.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Seoul, South Korea
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Seoul, South Korea

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Incheon International Airport at 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, then take the AREX (Airport Railroad Express) to Seoul Station for approximately 8,000 KRW. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and settle in for the night.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night snack at a 24-hour convenience store (GS25 or CU) near the hotel - try triangle kimbap and ramen for under 3,000 KRW

day_by_day.notes: Keep your T-money card purchase in mind at the airport - it costs 2,500 KRW and can be loaded with cash to use on all public transit throughout Seoul. Exchange some currency at the airport for better rates.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from jet lag. Head to a nearby local bakery or café for a light breakfast. Explore the immediate neighborhood around the hotel to get your bearings and pick up any essentials from a local mart.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Gyeongbokgung Palace (admission: 3,000 KRW), Seoul's largest and most iconic royal palace. Rent a hanbok (traditional Korean dress) near the palace gates for around 10,000-15,000 KRW for free palace entry while wearing it. Explore the palace grounds and the National Folk Museum of Korea (free entry within palace grounds).
day_by_day.evening: Walk through Bukchon Hanok Village, a stunning neighborhood of traditional Korean hanok houses. Stroll through the narrow alleyways and enjoy the atmospheric evening views. Head to Insadong for dinner and street food exploration.

meals.breakfast: Local bakery or convenience store near hotel - around 3,000-5,000 KRW
meals.lunch: Gimbap restaurant near Gyeongbokgung - try a set meal for 5,000-7,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Insadong street food - try hotteok (sweet pancakes), tteokbokki, and odeng for under 8,000 KRW total

day_by_day.notes: December in Seoul is cold (around -5°C to 5°C), so dress in warm layers. The palace closes on Tuesdays, so check the schedule. Gyeongbokgung is closed on Tuesdays.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace and its famous Secret Garden (Huwon). The combined ticket costs 8,000 KRW. The Secret Garden tour is guided and runs at set times, so arrive early to secure a spot. This UNESCO World Heritage Site is stunning even in winter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Jongno-gu area and visit Jogyesa Temple, the head temple of Korean Buddhism (free entry). The temple is beautifully decorated in December. Walk to nearby Cheonggyecheon Stream, a restored urban waterway perfect for a scenic afternoon stroll.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Gwangjang Market, one of Seoul's oldest and most famous traditional markets. This is a must for food lovers - try bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), yukhoe (beef tartare), and mayak kimbap. Budget around 10,000-15,000 KRW for a filling market dinner.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or local café near hotel - 3,000-5,000 KRW
meals.lunch: Affordable set lunch near Changdeokgung - doenjang jjigae (soybean paste stew) set for 7,000-9,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Gwangjang Market food stalls - 10,000-15,000 KRW for a variety of dishes

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Garden tour at Changdeokgung requires advance booking during peak seasons. Book online at the official palace website. Wear very warm clothing as the garden tour involves significant outdoor walking.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Hongdae, Seoul's vibrant youth culture and K-indie music district. Explore the street art, quirky shops, and the lively morning atmosphere. Visit the Hongik University area and browse the unique boutiques and vintage shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short bus to Sinchon and Ewha Womans University area. The campus is architecturally interesting and the surrounding streets are filled with affordable fashion, beauty shops, and cafés. Explore the underground shopping arcade for budget K-fashion finds.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hongdae for the evening live music scene. Many small clubs and venues host affordable or free live performances featuring indie K-pop, jazz, and rock. Check out the free street performances near Hongdae entrance. Explore the night market stalls for snacks.

meals.breakfast: Café in Hongdae - Americano and toast for around 5,000-7,000 KRW
meals.lunch: Affordable Korean restaurant in Sinchon - budae jjigae (army stew) for 8,000-10,000 KRW per person
meals.dinner: Hongdae street food and pojangmacha (street tent bar) - tteokbokki, fried chicken, and makgeolli for 12,000-15,000 KRW

day_by_day.notes: Hongdae is one of the best places in Seoul to experience K-culture firsthand. Look for flyers advertising free or low-cost live music events. Many indie artists perform here on weekends and weekday evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Visit N Seoul Tower (Namsan Tower) in the morning for panoramic views of Seoul. Take the Namsan Cable Car (9,500 KRW round trip) or hike up the trail for free. The tower observatory admission is 16,000 KRW, but the surrounding park and love lock area are free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Itaewon, Seoul's most international neighborhood. Browse the diverse shops, vintage clothing stores, and antique markets along Antique Furniture Street. Visit Leeum Samsung Museum of Art nearby (admission varies, some sections free).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Myeongdong, Seoul's premier shopping and street food district. The evening street food scene is incredible - try Korean corn dogs, egg bread (gyeran-ppang), grilled skewers, and more. Browse cosmetic stores like Innisfree and The Face Shop for affordable K-beauty products.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area café or convenience store - 3,000-5,000 KRW
meals.lunch: Itaewon international food street - shawarma or Korean-fusion for 8,000-12,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Myeongdong street food extravaganza - budget 10,000-15,000 KRW for a variety of snacks and small dishes

day_by_day.notes: Myeongdong is extremely crowded in the evenings but the street food is worth it. Many cosmetic stores offer free samples and have staff who speak multiple languages. December evenings are very cold so dress warmly for outdoor street food eating.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress, a UNESCO World Heritage Site about 1 hour from Seoul by subway (Line 1 to Suwon Station, then bus). The fortress walls and gates are free to walk, with a small admission fee of 1,000 KRW for the main palace area. The morning light on the fortress walls is beautiful.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Suwon's traditional market near the fortress. Visit Haenggung Palace (admission 1,500 KRW) within the fortress complex. Walk the full fortress wall circuit (approximately 5.7 km) for stunning views of the city.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul and head to Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), a futuristic architectural landmark designed by Zaha Hadid. The exterior is free to admire and photograph. Explore the surrounding Dongdaemun shopping district and night markets that stay open until dawn.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store near hotel - 3,000-5,000 KRW
meals.lunch: Suwon traditional market - famous Suwon galbi (grilled short ribs) or affordable market food for 8,000-12,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Dongdaemun area pojangmacha or 24-hour restaurant - sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) for 7,000-9,000 KRW

day_by_day.notes: Suwon Hwaseong Fortress is one of the best day trips from Seoul and very budget-friendly. The subway ride is covered by your T-money card. Wear comfortable walking shoes as the fortress wall walk involves significant elevation changes.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan (free admission). This is one of the largest museums in Asia with an incredible collection of Korean artifacts spanning thousands of years. Allow at least 2-3 hours to explore the main exhibitions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the nearby War Memorial of Korea (free admission). This sobering but important museum provides deep insight into Korean history and the Korean War. The outdoor exhibits of military equipment are impressive and free to explore.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Gangnam district for the evening. Visit the famous Garosu-gil (Tree-lined Street) for window shopping and café hopping. Experience the contrast between trendy Gangnam and traditional Seoul. Try to find a local Korean BBQ restaurant for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Local café near hotel - 4,000-6,000 KRW
meals.lunch: Museum cafeteria at National Museum of Korea - affordable set meals for 7,000-9,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Budget Korean BBQ in Gangnam area - samgyeopsal (pork belly) restaurant for 12,000-15,000 KRW per person including sides

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum of Korea is closed on Mondays. Both museums are within walking distance of each other in Yongsan. The War Memorial is particularly moving and educational for understanding Korean culture and modern history.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Lotte World, one of the world's largest indoor theme parks, or explore the free outdoor Magic Island area and Seokchon Lake for a budget-friendly alternative. The lake area is beautifully lit during winter. Stroll around the lake and enjoy the festive December atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to nearby Jamsil area and visit the Olympic Park (free entry), built for the 1988 Seoul Olympics. The park has interesting sculptures, sports facilities, and the KSPO Dome. Walk through the peaceful grounds and visit the Olympic Museum.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Jamsil's local food scene. Visit the underground shopping centers and try the local restaurants. Head to a norebang (Korean karaoke room) for a quintessential K-culture experience. Private rooms typically cost 15,000-20,000 KRW per hour for a group.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store near hotel - 3,000-5,000 KRW
meals.lunch: Affordable restaurant near Olympic Park - kimchi jjigae (kimchi stew) set for 7,000-9,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Jamsil local restaurant street - try dakgalbi (spicy stir-fried chicken) for 10,000-13,000 KRW per person

day_by_day.notes: Norebang is a must-do K-culture experience. Look for noraebangs with time-based pricing rather than per-song pricing for better value. Many offer free drinks or snacks with room rental. This is a great social activity perfect for meeting other travelers.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Namdaemun Market, one of Korea's oldest and largest traditional markets. Open since 1414, this sprawling market sells everything from clothing and accessories to food and kitchenware at very affordable prices. Arrive early for the best selection and atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Seoul City Hall and the surrounding Deoksugung Palace (admission 1,000 KRW). The palace has a beautiful stone wall road (Deoksugung Doldam-gil) that is famous for its romantic atmosphere. Explore the modern Seoul Plaza and the surrounding cultural district.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Cheonggyecheon Stream for the evening light festival (usually held in winter). The stream is beautifully illuminated and the walk along the stream is free and magical in December. End the evening in the nearby Euljiro area, known for its hipster cafés and bars.

meals.breakfast: Namdaemun Market breakfast - try kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup) for 6,000-8,000 KRW
meals.lunch: Namdaemun Market food stalls - hoddeok, gimbap, and sundae (blood sausage) for 5,000-8,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Euljiro area local restaurant - affordable Korean set meal for 8,000-12,000 KRW

day_by_day.notes: Namdaemun Market is excellent for buying Korean souvenirs at wholesale prices. Bargaining is acceptable here. The market is very crowded on weekends. Deoksugung Palace has a changing of the guard ceremony that is worth watching if timing aligns.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Eve! Visit Jogyesa Temple in the morning to see the beautiful lantern decorations. Then head to Insadong for morning tea at a traditional Korean tea house. Browse the artisan shops and galleries in this cultural street.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Seoul Museum of History (free admission) near Gyeongbokgung to learn about Seoul's transformation from ancient capital to modern metropolis. The museum has excellent English signage and interactive exhibits.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Christmas Eve in Seoul! Myeongdong and Gangnam are beautifully decorated with Christmas lights and festivities. Join the crowds for street food and festive shopping. Many churches in Seoul hold special Christmas Eve services open to visitors. The city has a magical atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Korean tea house in Insadong - tea and rice cake set for 8,000-10,000 KRW
meals.lunch: Insadong restaurant - bibimbap set for 9,000-11,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve street food in Myeongdong - treat yourself to a slightly larger budget of 15,000-20,000 KRW for the festive occasion

day_by_day.notes: Seoul celebrates Christmas enthusiastically as a significant portion of the population is Christian. The city is beautifully decorated and the festive atmosphere is wonderful. Many stores and restaurants have special Christmas promotions. Book any restaurant dinners in advance as Christmas Eve is very busy.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Day in Seoul! Visit Bukhansan National Park for a morning hike. The park is accessible by subway (Gupabal or Dobongsan stations) and offers stunning winter hiking with snow-dusted peaks. The hike to Baegundae Peak is challenging but rewarding. Entry to the park is free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from hiking and visit a local jjimjilbang (Korean sauna/bathhouse) to warm up and relax. A jjimjilbang is a deeply cultural Korean experience - entry typically costs 10,000-15,000 KRW and includes access to hot baths, saunas, and common rest areas where you can sleep.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate Christmas evening with a special Korean BBQ dinner. Many restaurants have Christmas specials. Head to a popular samgyeopsal (pork belly) restaurant and enjoy the communal grilling experience with soju or Korean beer.

meals.breakfast: Pack snacks from convenience store for the hike - 3,000-5,000 KRW
meals.lunch: Mountain trail snacks or restaurant near park entrance - ramyeon or kimbap for 5,000-8,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Christmas Korean BBQ - splurge slightly at 15,000-20,000 KRW per person including drinks

day_by_day.notes: Bukhansan National Park is one of the most visited national parks in the world due to its proximity to Seoul. In December, ice and snow can make trails slippery, so wear hiking boots with good grip. The jjimjilbang experience is uniquely Korean and not to be missed - bring a change of clothes.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the vibrant Hongdae flea market area and explore the weekly Hope Market (check schedule as it varies seasonally). Browse independent designer goods, vintage items, and handmade crafts. This is great for unique, affordable souvenirs and experiencing the creative youth culture of Seoul.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Han River (Hangang) for an afternoon walk. The riverside parks are free and offer beautiful views of the city. Rent a bicycle (around 3,000 KRW per hour) to explore the riverside paths. Visit Yeouido Hangang Park, popular with locals year-round.
day_by_day.evening: Spend your second-to-last evening in the Mapo area near the Han River. Visit the local craft beer bars or makgeolli (Korean rice wine) houses for an authentic evening experience. Try a traditional Korean pojangmacha for street food and drinks under a tent.

meals.breakfast: Café near hotel - coffee and pastry for 5,000-7,000 KRW
meals.lunch: Han River convenience store picnic - a very Korean experience! CU or GS25 sells cup noodles, kimbap, and snacks. Budget 5,000-8,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Mapo area restaurant - haemul pajeon (seafood pancake) and makgeolli for 12,000-15,000 KRW

day_by_day.notes: Eating cup noodles by the Han River is a beloved Korean tradition even in winter! Convenience stores near the river have hot water dispensers and seating areas. The Han River parks have outdoor heaters in some areas during winter. Use this day for any last-minute souvenir shopping.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Seoul! Revisit any favorite spots or neighborhoods you want to see one last time. Head back to Gyeongbokgung area for a final photo session or visit any museums you may have missed. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping at Insadong or Namdaemun Market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin preparing for departure. Pack your bags and check out of the hotel. Head to Seoul Station to take the AREX to Incheon Airport. Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. The AREX express train takes about 43 minutes (9,500 KRW) or the all-stop train takes about 66 minutes (4,150 KRW).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Incheon International Airport. Enjoy one final Korean meal at the airport - the food court has affordable options including Korean set meals for 8,000-12,000 KRW. Browse the duty-free shops for any last-minute Korean cosmetics or snacks to bring home.

meals.breakfast: Final Korean breakfast near hotel - haejang-guk (hangover soup) or seolleongtang (ox bone soup) for 8,000-10,000 KRW
meals.lunch: Quick lunch near Seoul Station or at the airport - convenience store or food court for 7,000-10,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Airport food court or take snacks on board - 8,000-12,000 KRW

day_by_day.notes: Seoul Station has luggage storage if you want to explore a bit before heading to the airport. The AREX has a city check-in service at Seoul Station where you can check your bags and receive your boarding pass before heading to the airport - highly recommended! Keep some Korean Won for transport to the airport and any last purchases.

trip_options.title: Classic Seoul, South Korea Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Seoul, South Korea

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Incheon International Airport at 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, collect baggage, and take the AREX Express Train or airport limousine bus to central Seoul. Check into Aegean Bliss Resort and settle in.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at airport
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack at a nearby 24-hour convenience store (GS25 or CU) — try triangle kimbap, ramen, or hotteok to get your first taste of Korean snack culture

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — you've had a long flight. Hydrate well and get to bed early to beat jet lag. Exchange some currency at the airport or use a Wise/Revolut card. Pick up a T-money transit card at the airport for easy subway access throughout your trip.

day_by_day.morning: Start your Seoul journey with a visit to Gyeongbokgung Palace, the grandest of Seoul's Five Grand Palaces. Arrive early (opens 9:00 AM) to beat crowds. Watch the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony at 10:00 AM and explore the palace grounds, including Geunjeongjeon Hall and the scenic Gyeonghoeru Pavilion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk north to Bukchon Hanok Village, a beautifully preserved neighborhood of traditional Korean hanok houses. Stroll the winding alleys, admire the tile-roofed homes, and enjoy panoramic views of the city. Then explore the nearby Insadong district — browse traditional crafts, tea houses, and art galleries along the main street.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Insadong's Ssamziegil courtyard for artisan shops and street food. Enjoy dinner in the area and then take a leisurely evening walk around the neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby café — try a Korean-style breakfast of doenjang jjigae (soybean paste soup) and rice at a local eatery
meals.lunch: Tosokchon Samgyetang near Gyeongbokgung — famous for ginseng chicken soup (samgyetang), a warming and nourishing dish perfect for December
meals.dinner: Insadong Teahouse Street — dine at a traditional Korean restaurant offering bibimbap or japchae, followed by a cup of traditional yuja-cha (yuzu tea)

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung is free on the last Wednesday of each month. Dress warmly — December in Seoul averages -2°C to 4°C. Hanbok rental is available near the palace entrance for a fun cultural experience and free palace entry.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace and its famous UNESCO-listed Secret Garden (Huwon). Book the Secret Garden tour in advance as spots are limited. The garden is magical in winter with frosted pines and traditional pavilions dusted in snow.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Jongno-gu area, heading to Tapgol Park and then down to Cheonggyecheon Stream — a beautifully restored urban waterway perfect for a scenic afternoon walk. The stream is often decorated with winter light installations in December.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) for its iconic futuristic architecture. Browse the surrounding Dongdaemun shopping district, which comes alive at night. The area is famous for its fashion markets and street food stalls.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local bakery — Paris Baguette or Tous Les Jours for pastries and coffee
meals.lunch: Gwangjang Market near Jongno — one of Seoul's oldest traditional markets. Try bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak kimbap (sesame rice rolls), and yukhoe (beef tartare)
meals.dinner: Dongdaemun area — enjoy dakgalbi (spicy stir-fried chicken) at a local restaurant, followed by street food like tteokbokki and eomuk (fish cake skewers) at outdoor stalls

day_by_day.notes: Gwangjang Market is a must-visit for authentic local food culture. Secret Garden tours run at set times — book online via the official palace website. Cheonggyecheon Stream has a lovely winter lantern festival in December.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Myeongdong, Seoul's premier shopping and beauty district. Explore the main pedestrian street lined with K-beauty shops (Innisfree, Etude House, Olive Young), international brands, and street food vendors. Stock up on skincare and cosmetics at mid-range prices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk uphill to Namsan Mountain and take the Namsan Cable Car up to N Seoul Tower (Namsan Tower). Enjoy panoramic views of the city from the observation deck. Add a love lock to the famous fence and explore the surrounding Namsan Park.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Myeongdong for dinner and evening street food. The street food scene here is vibrant — perfect for trying a variety of Korean snacks in one place.

meals.breakfast: Myeongdong Kyoja near the main street — famous for kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup) and mandu (dumplings), a hearty breakfast option
meals.lunch: Street food lunch in Myeongdong — try tornado potato, hotteok (sweet pancakes), corn dogs, and tteokbokki from various stalls
meals.dinner: Myeongdong area — visit a Korean BBQ restaurant for samgyeopsal (grilled pork belly) with all the banchan (side dishes). Budget around ₩15,000–25,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Myeongdong is extremely busy on Friday evenings. N Seoul Tower observation deck entry costs around ₩16,000. The cable car runs frequently and costs about ₩9,500 round trip. December evenings are very cold on the mountain — dress in layers.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan — one of Asia's largest museums and completely free to enter. Explore thousands of years of Korean history, art, and artifacts across beautifully curated galleries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Itaewon, Seoul's most international neighborhood. Walk down Antique Furniture Street (Itaewon-daero 55ga-gil), explore the eclectic boutiques, and visit the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art for world-class contemporary and traditional Korean art.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Itaewon for the evening — the neighborhood transforms into a lively social hub after dark. Explore Haebangchon (HBC) neighborhood nearby for a more local, bohemian vibe with indie bars and cozy restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a traditional Korean breakfast restaurant near your accommodation
meals.lunch: National Museum of Korea café or nearby — try dosirak (Korean lunch box) style meal
meals.dinner: Itaewon — explore the diverse dining options. Try a Korean-fusion restaurant or enjoy authentic Korean fried chicken (chimaek) with a cold beer at a local chimaek bar

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum of Korea is free and open Tuesday–Sunday. Leeum Museum entry costs around ₩10,000–20,000. Itaewon is very multicultural and great for experiencing how K-culture intersects with global influences. Saturday nights here are lively.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning trip to Bukhansan National Park on the northern edge of Seoul. Hike the Bukhansanseong Fortress Trail — a moderate hike with stunning views of Seoul's skyline framed by granite peaks. The trail takes 3–4 hours for a full loop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city and head to the trendy Hongdae neighborhood — Seoul's youth culture and indie arts hub. Explore street art, browse vinyl record shops, vintage clothing stores, and quirky indie boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Hongdae for the evening. The area is famous for its nightlife, live music performances, and K-pop busking culture. Check out the main pedestrian street for street performers and live acts.

meals.breakfast: Pack a convenience store breakfast for the hike — triangle kimbap, banana milk, and a warm canned coffee
meals.lunch: Post-hike meal near Bukhansan or back in the city — doenjang jjigae set meal at a local restaurant to replenish energy
meals.dinner: Hongdae — try mapo tofu stew or sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) at a local spot, followed by bingsu (shaved ice dessert) or hotteok from a street stall

day_by_day.notes: Bukhansan hike requires proper footwear — trail can be icy in December. Wear hiking boots and bring hand warmers. Hongdae is best experienced in the afternoon and evening when the area is most vibrant. Sunday evenings here are particularly lively with street performances.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the hip and trendy Seongsu-dong neighborhood, often called 'Seoul's Brooklyn.' Visit artisan coffee roasteries, converted factory spaces turned into galleries and boutiques, and the famous Seoul Forest nearby — a beautiful urban park perfect for a winter morning stroll.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the COEX Mall in Gangnam — one of Asia's largest underground shopping malls. Visit the stunning Starfield Library inside the mall, browse the aquarium, and explore the extensive retail and entertainment complex.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Gangnam for the evening. Visit Gangnam Station area for dinner and experience the upscale side of Seoul that inspired the famous PSY song. Explore the underground shopping arcades.

meals.breakfast: Seongsu-dong specialty coffee roastery — try a hand-drip coffee with a Korean-style egg sandwich or croissant
meals.lunch: Seongsu-dong — try a trendy brunch spot or a local gukbap (rice soup) restaurant for a hearty mid-day meal
meals.dinner: Gangnam — enjoy galbi (grilled short ribs) at a mid-range Korean BBQ restaurant, or try a modern Korean cuisine restaurant for a slightly elevated dining experience

day_by_day.notes: Seongsu-dong is Seoul's most Instagram-worthy neighborhood right now. Seoul Forest is free and beautiful in winter. Starfield Library in COEX is free to visit and makes for stunning photos. COEX Aquarium entry is around ₩29,000.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the War Memorial of Korea in Yongsan — a powerful and moving museum documenting Korean history from ancient times through the Korean War and beyond. The outdoor exhibits of military equipment are impressive even in winter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Namdaemun Market — one of Seoul's oldest and largest traditional markets, dating back to 1414. Browse stalls selling everything from clothing and accessories to dried goods, street food, and traditional items. Great for picking up souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Lotte World Tower area in Jamsil. Visit the observation deck (Seoul Sky) on the 117th–123rd floors for breathtaking nighttime city views. The tower is especially beautiful with holiday lights in December.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby haejang-guk (hangover soup) restaurant — a beloved Korean morning tradition with a hearty bone broth soup
meals.lunch: Namdaemun Market — enjoy gejang (marinated raw crab), kalguksu, or freshly made hotteok from market vendors
meals.dinner: Jamsil area near Lotte World Tower — try a jokbal (braised pig's trotters) restaurant or a modern Korean restaurant in the Lotte World Mall food court

day_by_day.notes: War Memorial of Korea is free to enter. Seoul Sky observation deck costs around ₩27,000. Book tickets online in advance to avoid queues. December evenings offer spectacular views of the city lights from the top of the tower.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to the ancient city of Gyeongju (accessible by KTX bullet train, about 2 hours from Seoul Station). Visit Bulguksa Temple — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of Korea's most beautiful Buddhist temples, surrounded by pine forests.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Seokguram Grotto (a short bus ride from Bulguksa) — another UNESCO site featuring a stunning granite Buddhist shrine. Then visit the Gyeongju National Museum to learn about the Silla Kingdom's incredible history and treasures.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul by KTX. Arrive back in Seoul by 9–10 PM. Enjoy a light dinner near your hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Seoul Station before boarding the KTX — try a Korean-style breakfast set
meals.lunch: Gyeongju — try ssambap (rice and vegetables wrapped in leaves) or the famous Gyeongju bread (Gyeongju-ppang, a red bean pastry) as a local specialty
meals.dinner: Light dinner near hotel upon return — Korean convenience store meal or a nearby pojangmacha (street food tent) for tteokbokki and ramen

day_by_day.notes: KTX tickets should be booked in advance via the Korail website. Round trip costs approximately ₩50,000–70,000. Bulguksa and Seokguram entry fees are around ₩5,000–6,000 each. This is a long day — wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple in central Seoul — the head temple of Korean Buddhism and beautifully decorated with lanterns year-round. Enjoy the peaceful atmosphere and learn about Korean Buddhist culture. Nearby, explore the Bukchon Hanok Village once more at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Lotte Department Store or Shinsegae Department Store in Myeongdong to experience a Korean Christmas Eve — these stores go all out with decorations, live performances, and festive displays. Browse the luxury food halls for unique Korean holiday treats.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve in Seoul is a major celebration! Join the festive atmosphere in Myeongdong or Cheonggyecheon Stream, which is lit up beautifully. Many Seoulites celebrate Christmas Eve as a couple's holiday with elaborate light displays throughout the city.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — treat yourself on Christmas Eve
meals.lunch: Myeongdong — try a festive set meal at a mid-range Korean restaurant or explore the department store food halls
meals.dinner: Special Christmas Eve dinner — book a table at a well-regarded Korean restaurant in advance. Try a hansik (Korean royal cuisine) restaurant for a memorable experience. Budget ₩30,000–50,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve in Seoul is very festive and romantic. Myeongdong and city centers are packed with couples and families. Cheonggyecheon Stream light festival is at its peak during this period. Make dinner reservations well in advance. Many Koreans celebrate with fried chicken and cake — a beloved local tradition!

day_by_day.morning: Take a relaxed Christmas morning stroll through Gyeonghuigung Palace — the quietest of Seoul's palaces and often overlooked by tourists. Combine with a visit to the Seoul Museum of History next door, which offers fascinating exhibits on the city's transformation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Euljiro district — Seoul's hidden creative hub in a grid of old printing shops, hardware stores, and retro cafés. This area has been transformed into one of the city's most interesting cultural spaces with indie galleries and unique coffee shops hidden among the industrial buildings.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Banpo Bridge for the famous Moonlight Rainbow Fountain show (check seasonal schedule) or simply enjoy the Han River waterfront. Wrap up the evening with a relaxed dinner and perhaps a norebang (karaoke) session — the quintessential Korean evening activity.

meals.breakfast: Korean-style Christmas breakfast — try a local bakery for holiday pastries or a café for a festive brunch set
meals.lunch: Euljiro area — try a hidden gem local restaurant serving doenjang jjigae and banchan in a retro setting
meals.dinner: Korean Christmas tradition — order chimaek (fried chicken and beer) for delivery or at a local restaurant, followed by a Christmas cake from a Korean bakery (a beloved local tradition)

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Day is a public holiday in South Korea. Many attractions are open but some smaller shops may be closed. Norebang (karaoke rooms) are a must-try Korean cultural experience — rooms are private and rented by the hour, typically ₩15,000–30,000 per hour.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Folk Museum of Korea (located within Gyeongbokgung Palace grounds) for a deep dive into traditional Korean daily life, customs, and folk culture. The outdoor exhibits with traditional village reconstructions are particularly interesting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Mangwon Market in Mapo-gu — a beloved local traditional market that's become a foodie destination. Less touristy than Gwangjang, this market gives an authentic glimpse into everyday Seoul life. Then explore the Mangwon and Hapjeong neighborhoods for independent cafés and local shops.
day_by_day.evening: Final big evening in Seoul — head to the Hangang (Han River) Park for a classic Seoul experience. Rent a bicycle, enjoy the riverside views, and grab street food from the riverside vendors. End the night at a rooftop bar in Mapo or Hongdae for farewell drinks with a city view.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Korean breakfast near Gyeongbokgung — try sundubu jjigae or a kongnamul gukbap (bean sprout rice soup)
meals.lunch: Mangwon Market — feast on a variety of street foods: tteokbokki, soondae (blood sausage), pajeon (green onion pancakes), and fresh fruit
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a well-regarded Korean BBQ restaurant — splurge slightly on premium wagyu-style Korean beef (hanwoo) for a memorable last full dinner. Budget ₩40,000–60,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Mangwon Market is best on weekends when it's most lively. Han River Park is free and open 24 hours. Bicycle rental at the river costs around ₩3,000 per hour. This is a great day to do any last-minute shopping for gifts and souvenirs — Korean snacks, teas, beauty products, and traditional crafts make excellent gifts.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final leisurely Korean breakfast near your hotel. Take a last morning walk around your neighborhood to soak in the Seoul atmosphere. Do any final packing and check out of the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure time, visit any remaining spots on your list — perhaps a final stop at Olive Young for last-minute beauty purchases, or a farewell coffee at a specialty café. Head to Incheon International Airport via AREX Express Train (43 minutes from Seoul Station) or airport limousine bus.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Seoul. Browse the extensive duty-free shopping at Incheon Airport — one of the world's best airports with excellent food, cultural exhibits, and shopping. Enjoy a final Korean meal at the airport before boarding.

meals.breakfast: Final Korean breakfast — try a local restaurant for kimchi jjigae (kimchi stew) and rice, a warm and comforting send-off meal
meals.lunch: Light lunch near hotel or at the airport — airport food courts have excellent Korean options at reasonable prices
meals.dinner: Airport dinner before departure — try the Korean restaurant options in the departure terminal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your international flight for check-in and security at Incheon. The airport has a Korean Cultural Street with free cultural performances and exhibits if you have time to spare. Pick up last-minute gifts at the duty-free — Korean spirits (soju, makgeolli), teas, and snacks are popular choices. Safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Seoul, South Korea Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Seoul, South Korea

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Incheon International Airport at 22:30 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities — flight arrives late evening
day_by_day.evening: Private airport transfer via luxury chauffeur service to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check-in, unwind in your premium beachfront suite, and enjoy a late-night welcome amenity prepared by the hotel. Light exploration of the resort facilities and a relaxing nightcap at the hotel lounge bar.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit
meals.dinner: Late-night room service or hotel lounge dining featuring premium Korean snacks, seasonal fruits, and a curated selection of Korean traditional teas or premium soju cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day — rest and recovery is the priority. Confirm concierge arrangements for the following days. Tip: request a turndown service with a traditional Korean herbal pillow mist for a restorative first night.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late start with a premium hotel breakfast. Afterward, take a private guided orientation walk around the resort's surrounding neighborhood to acclimatize to Seoul's winter atmosphere. Visit a nearby traditional Korean tea house for a ceremonial morning tea experience featuring premium Jeju green tea and seasonal rice cakes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private chauffeur-driven tour to Gyeongbokgung Palace — Seoul's most iconic royal palace. Enjoy a VIP guided tour with a cultural historian explaining the Joseon Dynasty's history, architecture, and royal ceremonies. Explore the adjacent National Folk Museum of Korea for a curated deep-dive into Korean cultural heritage.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner reservation at Gaon (three Michelin-starred Korean fine dining) in Gangnam — experience a multi-course royal Korean cuisine tasting menu inspired by Joseon Dynasty court food, paired with premium Korean makgeolli and traditional herbal liquors.

meals.breakfast: Premium hotel breakfast buffet featuring Korean and Western selections — doenjang jjigae, japchae, fresh seasonal fruits, artisan breads, and barista-crafted coffee
meals.lunch: Traditional Korean set lunch at Tosokchon Samgyetang — legendary ginseng chicken soup in a historic hanok setting near Gyeongbokgung
meals.dinner: Gaon Restaurant — Michelin three-star royal Korean cuisine tasting menu (advance reservation essential)

day_by_day.notes: December in Seoul is cold (around -2°C to 5°C) — dress in warm, stylish layers. The palace grounds are stunning dusted with winter frost. Book Gaon at least 2–3 weeks in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private hanbok (traditional Korean dress) fitting and styling session at a premium hanbok atelier in Bukchon Hanok Village. Stroll through the beautifully preserved 600-year-old village in your hanbok with a personal photographer for a curated cultural photo session among the traditional tile-roofed houses.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Insadong — Seoul's premier cultural and antique district. Visit premium art galleries, traditional craft shops, and pick up bespoke Korean ceramics, hanji paper goods, and artisan souvenirs. Stop at Ssamziegil courtyard for a curated artisan market experience. Private calligraphy lesson with a master calligrapher.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private performance of traditional Korean music and dance (Gugak) at the National Theater of Korea, followed by dinner at Mingles — a Michelin-starred restaurant blending Korean flavors with global techniques.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby premium café — Korean-style porridge (juk) with premium side dishes
meals.lunch: Lunch at Balwoo Gongyang — Michelin-starred temple food restaurant in Insadong, featuring exquisite Buddhist vegetarian cuisine
meals.dinner: Mingles Restaurant — Michelin-starred modern Korean cuisine with an exceptional wine and soju pairing menu

day_by_day.notes: Hanbok rental packages with professional photography typically run 2–3 hours. Book the calligraphy session and Gugak performance in advance through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Changdeokgung Palace and the UNESCO-listed Secret Garden (Huwon) — a breathtaking royal garden with ancient pavilions, frozen lotus ponds, and centuries-old trees dusted in winter frost. An exclusive early-morning access tour before general crowds arrive is highly recommended.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the prestigious Leeum Samsung Museum of Art in Itaewon — one of Asia's finest private art museums featuring Korean traditional art alongside contemporary global masterpieces. Explore the Antique Row (Itaewon Antique Furniture Street) for premium Korean antiques and art pieces.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private K-culture immersion experience: a behind-the-scenes tour of HYBE Insight (BTS and K-pop cultural museum) followed by dinner at Jungsik — a Michelin two-star restaurant offering avant-garde Korean cuisine with theatrical presentation.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full Korean morning spread with grilled fish, seasonal namul vegetables, miso soup, and premium rice
meals.lunch: Premium lunch at Pierre Gagnaire à Séoul in Lotte Hotel — French-Korean fusion by the legendary French chef
meals.dinner: Jungsik Restaurant — Michelin two-star modern Korean tasting menu with sommelier-guided wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Garden tour requires advance booking and has limited daily slots. HYBE Insight is extremely popular — book tickets well in advance through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury wellness morning: traditional Korean jjimjilbang (Korean bathhouse) experience at a premium spa facility — enjoy the full ritual of hot mineral pools, body scrub (Italy towel exfoliation), and traditional Korean sauna rooms (infrared, charcoal, salt). This is an authentic cultural wellness tradition.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Namdaemun Market and Gwangjang Market with a private food guide for an immersive Korean street food and gourmet market tour. Sample bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap, tteokbokki, and seasonal winter delicacies. Visit a premium Korean ginseng shop for high-grade red ginseng products.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cable car ride to Namsan Tower (N Seoul Tower) for panoramic winter city views — the city lights in December are spectacular. Enjoy a romantic dinner at the rotating N Grill restaurant at the top of the tower.

meals.breakfast: Light in-room breakfast or hotel café — fruit, yogurt, granola, and premium Korean teas before the spa morning
meals.lunch: Gourmet street food tour at Gwangjang Market — curated tasting of Seoul's most iconic market foods with a private guide
meals.dinner: N Grill at Namsan Tower — panoramic fine dining with contemporary Korean-European cuisine and exceptional wine list

day_by_day.notes: Book the premium jjimjilbang experience at a luxury facility like Siloam Sauna or Dragon Hill Spa VIP floor. The Namsan Tower dinner is best reserved for sunset timing — around 5:30 PM in December.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Hwaseong Fortress in Suwon via private chauffeur. Explore the magnificent 18th-century fortress walls, gates, and command posts with a private cultural guide. Walk the full fortress perimeter (approximately 5.7 km) for stunning winter landscape views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearby Korean Folk Village (Minsokchon) — a living museum recreating traditional Joseon-era village life with authentic performances, craft demonstrations, and seasonal winter festivals. Experience traditional Korean games and artisan workshops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul. Dinner at Ryunique — a celebrated fine dining restaurant offering a creative Korean-inspired tasting menu with theatrical storytelling elements and exceptional beverage pairings.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before early departure
meals.lunch: Traditional Korean royal court cuisine set meal at a premium restaurant in Suwon near Hwaseong Fortress
meals.dinner: Ryunique Restaurant — creative fine dining with Korean narrative tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: Suwon is approximately 45–60 minutes from central Seoul by private car. Dress in very warm layers — the fortress walls are exposed to winter winds. The Korean Folk Village has special winter programs in December.

day_by_day.morning: Immersive K-beauty and Korean skincare masterclass at a premium beauty studio in Gangnam — learn the legendary 10-step Korean skincare routine from expert aestheticians, receive personalized skin analysis, and enjoy a luxury facial treatment using top Korean skincare brands (Sulwhasoo, History of Whoo, O Hui).
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury shopping experience along Apgujeong Rodeo Street and Cheongdam-dong — Seoul's most prestigious luxury retail district. Visit flagship stores of Korean luxury brands (MCM, Gentle Monster, Ader Error) alongside global luxury houses. Stop at the iconic Dosan Park for a premium café experience.
day_by_day.evening: Private K-drama filming location tour of iconic Seoul neighborhoods — visit Bukchon, Ihwa Mural Village, and Cheonggyecheon Stream, beautifully illuminated with winter festival lights. Dinner at La Yeon — the Michelin three-star Korean restaurant at The Shilla Hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — Korean-style with premium additions
meals.lunch: Premium lunch at Alma by Mingoo Kang in Cheongdam — refined Korean cuisine in an elegant setting
meals.dinner: La Yeon at The Shilla Hotel — Michelin three-star traditional Korean haute cuisine (one of Seoul's most prestigious dining experiences)

day_by_day.notes: Book La Yeon well in advance — it is consistently one of the hardest reservations to secure in Seoul. The K-beauty masterclass should be arranged through the hotel concierge 3–4 days in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Joseon Royal Tombs (UNESCO World Heritage) — specifically the Seonjeongneung Royal Tombs in Gangnam, a serene and often overlooked gem of Korean heritage hidden within the modern city. A cultural historian will explain the significance of Confucian burial rites and royal traditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the DDP (Dongdaemun Design Plaza) — Zaha Hadid's iconic futuristic building — for a curated design and K-culture exhibition. Explore the adjacent Dongdaemun History and Culture Park. Visit the premium fabric and fashion district for bespoke Korean fashion shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a world-class performance at the Seoul Arts Center — check seasonal program for opera, ballet, or classical concert. Dinner at Dooreyoo — a celebrated modern Korean restaurant known for its innovative approach to traditional Korean flavors.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Stylish lunch at Cafe Onion Seongsu or a premium brunch spot in the trendy Seongsu-dong neighborhood (Seoul's Brooklyn) after the tomb visit
meals.dinner: Dooreyoo Restaurant — innovative modern Korean cuisine with a focus on seasonal and fermented ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Check the Seoul Arts Center program calendar in advance and book tickets through the hotel concierge. The Seonjeongneung Tombs are a peaceful contrast to the surrounding Gangnam skyscrapers — a uniquely Seoul experience.

day_by_day.morning: Private day trip to the DMZ (Demilitarized Zone) — one of the most unique and historically significant experiences in the world. A premium VIP DMZ tour includes Imjingak Park, the Third Infiltration Tunnel, Dora Observatory overlooking North Korea, and Dorasan Station. Guided by a specialist historian.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the DMZ experience with a visit to the Peace and Life Zone (PLZ) — a unique ecological sanctuary that has developed naturally in the buffer zone. Return to Seoul in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve Eve celebration dinner at Antique — a romantic, intimate fine dining restaurant in Itaewon known for its exceptional Korean-European tasting menus and curated natural wine list. The hotel may offer special pre-Christmas evening programming.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before DMZ departure (tours typically depart by 8:00 AM)
meals.lunch: Premium packed lunch prepared by the hotel or a curated lunch stop near Imjingak
meals.dinner: Antique Restaurant, Itaewon — intimate fine dining with Korean-European fusion and natural wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: DMZ tours require passport and advance booking — arrange at least 5–7 days in advance through a reputable premium tour operator. Photography restrictions apply at certain points. This is a deeply moving and historically profound experience.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Eve morning: Private traditional Korean cooking class with a master chef — learn to prepare iconic Korean dishes including kimchi, bulgogi, japchae, and tteok (rice cakes). The class takes place in a beautifully restored hanok kitchen setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Jogyesa Temple — the head temple of Korean Buddhism in central Seoul — for a special winter solstice and pre-Christmas temple experience. Participate in a premium temple stay lite program: meditation session, tea ceremony, and a monk-guided temple tour. The temple is beautifully decorated with thousands of lanterns.
day_by_day.evening: Special Christmas Eve gala dinner at the hotel or at a premier Seoul venue — many luxury hotels offer exceptional Christmas Eve multi-course dinners with live entertainment. Alternatively, book a private dining experience at Kwonsooksoo — a prestigious hanok-style Korean fine dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Enjoy dishes prepared during the morning cooking class as part of the experience
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve special gala dinner — hotel grand Christmas dinner or Kwonsooksoo Restaurant for an intimate premium Korean dining experience in a historic hanok

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve in Seoul is a major celebration — the city is beautifully decorated and lively. Book Christmas Eve dinner well in advance as premium venues fill up months ahead. Jogyesa Temple is free to enter and deeply culturally enriching.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas morning: Leisurely late start with a luxurious hotel Christmas brunch. Enjoy a private winter walk along Cheonggyecheon Stream — a beautifully lit urban waterway running through central Seoul, especially magical during the winter light festival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Lotte World Tower Sky Observatory (123 floors, 555 meters) — the tallest building in Korea — for breathtaking 360-degree views of Seoul on a clear winter day. Explore the adjacent Lotte World Mall for premium shopping and a visit to the Lotte World Theme Park if desired.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas dinner at Dine by Fine — a premium rooftop dining experience, or a special Christmas tasting menu at Onjium — a prestigious Korean fine dining restaurant known for preserving ancient royal and scholarly culinary traditions of the Joseon era.

meals.breakfast: Grand Christmas brunch at the hotel — premium spread with Korean and Western festive dishes, champagne, and seasonal desserts
meals.lunch: Light premium café lunch near Cheonggyecheon or Lotte World
meals.dinner: Onjium Restaurant — exquisite traditional Korean cuisine rooted in Joseon scholarly and royal culinary heritage (Christmas special menu)

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Day in Seoul is a national public holiday. Many attractions remain open. The Lotte World Tower Sky Observatory is stunning on clear days — check weather forecasts. Onjium requires advance booking and is considered one of Seoul's most culturally significant dining experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the National Museum of Korea — one of Asia's largest and most impressive museums. Explore the world-class collections of Korean art, history, and culture spanning 5,000 years, including the iconic Gilt-bronze Pensive Bodhisattva. A private curator-led tour provides an unparalleled depth of experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the trendy and artistic Seongsu-dong neighborhood — Seoul's creative hub. Visit premium concept stores, artisan coffee roasters, converted factory galleries, and bespoke leather workshops. Experience the unique energy of this rapidly evolving cultural district. Visit the popular Seoul Forest for a winter afternoon stroll.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell eve dinner at Mosu Seoul — a Michelin two-star restaurant offering an exceptional seasonal Korean tasting menu with a philosophy deeply rooted in Korean culinary tradition and premium local ingredients. Pair with a curated Korean natural wine and traditional liquor selection.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Premium brunch or lunch at a celebrated Seongsu-dong café-restaurant such as Onion Seongsu or a curated artisan dining spot
meals.dinner: Mosu Seoul — Michelin two-star seasonal Korean tasting menu (advance reservation essential)

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum of Korea is free to enter — a remarkable value for one of the world's great museums. Seongsu-dong is best explored on foot. This is an ideal day for final souvenir shopping and gift purchasing.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Seoul: Relaxed luxury hotel breakfast. Last-minute premium shopping at a nearby luxury department store (Shinsegae, Hyundai, or Galleria) or a final stroll through a favorite neighborhood. Visit a premium Korean tea shop for high-grade artisan teas and traditional confections to bring home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time — optional visit to a nearby cultural site or a final relaxing spa treatment at the hotel. Pack and prepare for checkout. Private chauffeur transfer to Incheon International Airport with ample time for premium lounge access and departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Incheon International Airport — enjoy the First Class or Business Class lounge facilities. Reflect on an extraordinary 13-day journey through Seoul's royal heritage, vibrant K-culture, world-class cuisine, and timeless traditions.

meals.breakfast: Final premium hotel breakfast — savor your last Korean morning meal with all the seasonal flavors
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at the hotel or airport premium lounge
meals.dinner: Airport premium lounge dining or in-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3.5–4 hours before international departure at Incheon. The airport is a destination in itself — explore the transit cultural zone, duty-free luxury shopping, and the Korean Cultural Street inside the terminal. Keep all receipts for VAT tax refund processing before departure.
